 Montgomery County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0046
 Billy Jones, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Billy Jones
Date:
March 11, 2024
Location:
Offices of Dunn & Acosta LLP
Examining attorney:
Marilyn Fox, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Candice Smith, Dunn & Acosta LLP
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd prefer to give my name as a placeholder for this exercise, so let's say Plaintiff Witness One.
Q: Understood. Plaintiff, where were you when the collision happened?
A: I was driving through a four-way intersection in Houston, Texas, heading east on a road with a green light.
Q: Can you describe what you saw as you entered the intersection?
A: A vheicle came from the cross street on my right side. I had the right of way, I believe. I tried to brake, but the other car struck
the driver's side of my vehicle before I could stop.
Q: How fast were you traveling at that point?
A: I'd say I was going the posted speed, maybe a little under it, because the light had just turned green and I was accelerating
gently.
Q: After the impact, what did you notice about your body?
A: My right shoulder hurt immediately. I was holding the steering wheel and felt a sharp pain when my arm was jerked. I couldn't
lift my arm above my shoulder without pain.
Q: Did you seek medical attention that day?
A: Yes. Paramedics checked me at the scene, and I was taken to an urgent care clinic later that afternoon for an X-ray and an
exam.
Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've been attending physical therapy about three times a week. I was also given a sling for a while and prescribed
anti-inflammatory medication. Recently, my doctor discussed whether I might need an injection if the therapy doesn't help.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily activities?
A: It's been hard. I used to coach my kid's soccer team on weekends, and I've had to hand that over to my wife. Simple things like
reaching for a shelf, combing my hair, or lifting groceries are difficult. I also had to stop my weekend woodworking hobby.
Q: Have you been able to return to your job?
A: I returned to work after a few weeks, but I'm on modified duty. I can't do the lifting I used to do, so I work mostly at a desk
now.
Q: Before this accident, did you have any prior problems with that shoulder?
A: No, not that I can recall. I was active and had no ongoing issues with it.
Q: Thank you. Nothing further at this time.
</page>
